text:
mike_p: Quick sync — we need to finalize SLO acceptance for Embeddings v1 before we lock launch scope. Customer X is pushing for p95 <= 200ms and enterprise SLA language. Any hard blockers?

ashley_pm: short answer: we can commit to p95 200ms for hosted tier with dedicated capacity, but hosted PAYG will need fallback rules. Need SRE signoff on error budget and fallback UX.

sam_sre: Agree. From infra side the risk is tail latency on cold KV-cache misses. Current numbers: p50 ~80ms, p95 ~220-260ms depending on seq len. I can put an ops mitigation: keep warmed pool for top 30% of traffic.

jess_eng: Implementation note — batching changes we planned for v1.2 drop p95 ~20-30ms but adds variability for single-request low-latency paths. Suggest tiered routing: small requests -> low-latency instances; bulk -> batched instances.

oliver_sales: Customers will accept 'best-effort' for PAYG but enterprise contracts want explicit SLA and a credit schedule. We should map tiers to SLA language now.

ashley_pm: Proposal: 1) Hosted PAYG: p95 latency target 250ms, documented degrade to 350ms during tail events; 2) Hosted Dedicated / Enterprise: p95 200ms SLA with error budget. Rollout gated by SRE checklist. Thoughts?

mike_p: That seems pragmatic. What are acceptance criteria for launch? Need concrete checks.

sam_sre: Acceptance checklist draft: 
- Load test: 1M req/day with 95th percentile under target for 48h
- Chaos: simulate KV eviction and cold-start spikes, observe graceful degrade behavior
- Observability: traces and token-level cost breakdown available in console routes
- Rollout: canary @5% traffic -> 25% -> 100% with automated rollback on error budget burn > 10%

jess_eng: Add entry for quantization fallback: if low-cost quantized model used, ensure semantic drift < 2% on evaluation prompts.

oliver_sales: Can we make fallback messaging explicit so customers know when they're on quantized/cheaper variant? Legal wants transparency.

ashley_pm: Yes. UX requirement: response header/meta with model_variant and degraded=true if fallback triggered. Also show in console.

sam_sre: Edge cases: long sequences (>4096) currently have different kernel path and p95 spikes. For launch we should either reject >4096 with 4xx or route to non-SLA best-effort pool. Prefer explicit reject for enterprise SLA.

jess_eng: Implementation example for reject: `if seq_len > 4096: return 413, "sequence too long for SLA tier"` — quick to ship.

mike_p: OK. Can someone capture this into the PRD acceptance criteria and RFC? I want the final doc to include the exact SLA wording and rollback playbook.

ashley_pm: I will draft PRD section — acceptance_criteria, rollout_steps, fallback_matrix, SLA_text. Ping me for review. ETA EOD Tue.

ci-bot: ci/canary-tests started for embeddings-v1-canary (build #482)

sam_sre: I'll schedule the load tests and add the chaos scenarios to the runbook. Will update results in this thread.

oliver_sales: FYI flagged to Customer X that enterprise SLA requires Dedicated capacity commitment; they okayed it but requested the credit terms.

mike_p: Perfect. Last ask: include a short decision log entry explaining why PAYG gets softer target. Helps future audits.

ashley_pm: noted — adding decision log + timestamped rationale.

jess_eng: small follow-up: need a code owner for the routing policy. Assign to @jess_eng unless someone objects.

sam_sre: no objections.

mike_p: Thanks team :thumbsup: We'll review PRD draft tomorrow at 10am.
